brief:
Providence, Rhode Island residents voted to divest the city's foreign investments from countries profiting from genocide, The Guardian reported. The ballot measure passed during last week's midterm elections, making Providence the second U.S. city to cut investment ties with Israel.

The referendum reflects growing momentum within the pro-Palestine movement across American municipalities. Providence joins an earlier city in taking such action through direct voter approval rather than municipal council decision-making.
dek: Voters in Providence, Rhode Island, chose to pull foreign investments from countries that profit from genocide The tectonic blue wave that washed over the country in last week’s midterms also brought about a historic night for the pro-Palestine movement.
title: Providence voters approve divestment from Israel over genocide concerns
